Figured out Forking as the way for DAO community to accomodate projects by fulfilling these needs: 

- irreconcilable and conflicting market thesis and management styles. 
- Apart from alleviating conflicts, it serves the purposes of reducing churn amongst actively contributing volunteers in our DAO community
- Forking ensures all prior contributors' efforts are ackowledged and equitably accounted in such situations
- creates more surface area for more volunteers to support DAO mission and purpose to fight "Fake News"
- reduce communication overhead and excessive efforts in aligning ever growing number of contributions in a project
- spreads DAO risk over multiple projects as opposed to consolidating all eggs in one basket (project)
- allow DAO to remain decentralized while still enjoying the benefit of a strong core leadership for each project

Soft forked project 
- Allows a parent project to "theorectically" sponsor a child project. 
- Contributions to a child project is still recorded on the parent project's ledger but labelled differently
- Contributions to the child project are still awarded governance tokens of the parent project
- Revenue generated by child project are held in the parent project vault

Hard forked project 
- Child project has claim independence of parent project
- Contributions to a child project is recorded on its own branced off version of the paren project's ledger
- Contributions to the child project are awarded governacen tokens in the child project.
- Revenue generated by child project are held in its own project vault

30 minutes face time to chat about the contextual framing of the conversations in the beer hall channel

The value of Beer Hall

- a place to surface unknown unknowns via discussion. A lot of the topics surfaced here ends up becoming trends that inform what potential projects to pursue next

- a place where members of the DAO can come together to get to interact with each other in a generally informal setting

-  a place where useful information about DAO operations can be surfaced, discussed upon and eventually voted upon

- a place where members can have visibility into the kind of value that is exchange hands between various DAO members. In other spaces, a lot of these kind of exchanges are done in privacy so other members who might be able to jump in to participate ends up missing out because they don't know the deal flow is happening. In fact most of the introductions I made, they are done here in this channel except those that have some NDA concerns in place.

*Proposed governance token management protocol*

The purpose of this protocol is to discourage excessive speculation on our governance tokens in the open market once it gets listed on Centralized exchanges while at the same time capitalize on market fluctuations to increased our fiat netbook value per issued governance token ratio



*_Rules_*
    - _*Rule 1*_: every quarter DAO will make provisions to increase governance tokens in circulation by 25% of what is already in circulation last day of the previous quarter. 

    - _*Rule 2*_: Full amount might not end up being circulated in the market if no exceptional price ranges present themselves 

    - _*Rule 3*_: DAO will make open market purchase as and when market value at which governance token is traded at falls below USDT net book value. 

    - _*Rule 4*_: DAO will make open market sales of governance tokens up to the total provision specified for market circulation as and when market value per token exceeds the minimal of either USDT1 or USDT net book value per token



*_Conclusion_* 
This protocol for governance token management when strictly adhered to in the long haul is anti-dilutive on nature. 

It has the effect of discouraging excessive speculation activities beyond desirable price range both on the upside and the downside 

The muting of speculative components in open market pricing of DAO governance token help curtail distractions DAO governance token holders might otherwise experience away from daily practice of Satseva

    _Rule 1_ - full amount of first initial sale in USD from buyer brought in by DAO, same exact amount is issued to DAO member who helped made the sale in TDG

I think this approach of directly serving samples of cacao to every single vendor at their booth suggested by Atelier is more well suited for such kinds of gatherings if the intention is to acquire vendors 

Might end up being more scalable than holding cacao circles directly targeting consumers since most consumers as observed is usually a one off hence the CAC (_customer acquisition cost_) versus the LTV (_customer life time value_) is not as positive on the _Return on Capital_ deployed 

To optimize the model, you want to drive down *_CAC*_ as much as possible and target demographics with the highest possible *_LTV X Conversion rates*_ multiple 

ideally if possible drive CAC down to Zero, hence why I have been spending time doing all the trash run to get pass the gates free of charge and systematically utilizing food banks to cut down food related operating expenses

[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 240
- Description: Agroverse Shop Updates
  
  Updates to the Agroverse shop:
  
  NEW EXPERIENCES ADDED
  Added two seasonal experiences to the Pacific West Coast journey where cacao is offered:
  
  • Slab City & Salvation Mountain - The Last Free Place in America
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/slab-city-salvation-mountain/index.html
  
  • Winter Desert Gatherings - Quartzite, Salton Sea & Joshua Tree
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/winter-desert-gatherings/index.html
  
  These gatherings (Tribe Boheme, Van Aid, SchooliePalooza, Bombay Beach Binnelie, Boondockers bash, Quartzite gem show, Rubber Tramp Rendezvous) occur during winter season (Thanksgiving through end of winter) and are now part of the journey map.
  
  TASTE PROFILE VISUALIZATIONS
  Added interactive taste profile charts to shipment pages. The inclusion of these taste graphs was inspired by noticing them on one of the cacao brands that Kirsten shared. Process:
  
  1. Took photos of taste profile sheets from CIC (Cacao Innovation Center)
  2. Used Grok to generate a detailed prompt
  3. Used that prompt with Cursor AI to generate the code
  4. Embedded interactive D3.js charts on each shipment page
  
  Taste profiles available on:
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl4/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl6/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl8/index.html
  
  COMMUNITY COLLABORATION
  Discussed taste profiling with Matheus. Since taste is subjective, we don't need to pay CIC for this. We have a community of chocolate makers and chocolatiers in San Francisco who can be involved in the process, making it more authentic and community-driven.
  
  THOUGHTS ON AI & WEB EVOLUTION
  Observations on web evolution:
  
  • Web 1.0 (Geocities era) - Rich, handcrafted pages, complex ecosystem
  • Web 1.5 (MySpace) - Mix of handcrafted and templated
  • Web 2.0 (Facebook) - Everything templatized for scale
  • Web 3.0 (AI era) - AI could handcraft pages, bringing back Web 1.0 richness without the heavy human lifting... the only question is a site fully ran based on this paradigm can it be scalable
  
  Experimenting with AI as a creative partner to build unique, handcrafted experiences at scale. The taste profile charts are an example - each tailored to the specific shipment without manually coding every one.

[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 120
- Description: Got this repository up and running so that future LLMs on other machines can easily come up to speed on context to handle various tasks within our DAO ecoystem
  
  https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/agentic_ai_context
  
  Basically human getting AIs to teach AIs so that humans dont need to teach again
  
  Started experimenting with the following come online based LLMs as opposed to cursor AI for eventual deployment to the cloud
  
  - Gemini CLI
  - ⁠Grok CLI
  - ⁠Claude CLI
  - ⁠Codex CLI
  
  Spent some time thinking through the architecture of how other RAG (_Retreival Augmentation Generation_) infrastructure have been set up 
  
  My sense is instead of incurring a bunch of server cost setting up a vector space database which we don’t really need at our scale as well as the simplicity of what we are doing 
  
  Pre-compile all our DAO’s knowledge based data as vectors and index them as flat files. 
  
  When we need the LLM to make specialized decisions within our context, just have one of the servers convert a query that is being passed in by the user into a vector and do a Euclidean comparison of the query versus all the other factors in the index files to retrieve the right contacts and then pass them to LLM we are utilizing to get the final result to return to the user.
  
  And if the data size becomes a little larger, we just shove the pre-compound vectors into an SQL light database, which is due a flat file that can be easily ported from one server to another. 
  
  Recurring modes of usage that I can think of 
  
  - on boarding of new prospective members
  - ⁠ existing members who wants to get caught up on what has happened in the DAO recently
  - ⁠ freight and shipping configurations
  - ⁠ production cost optimization configurations
  - ⁠ go to market and store outreach strategy
  - ⁠ stores re-stocking strategy
  - ⁠ social media content, marketing ongoing efforts and strategy
  
  My sense is once the stack is implemented. I got to spend less time on all this stuff that requires a lot of logic and just kinda mechanical and perhaps repetitive. 
  
  Instead spend more time on face-to-face interactions for business development and trust building purposes.

- Governance token

    - can be converted to utility tokens

    - has a 1 token to 1 vote voting weightage

    - Not entitled to dividends
    - can be freely bought and sold to facilitate game play
    - has a 1 token to 0.001 vote voting weightage

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
Figured out Forking as the way for DAO community to accomodate projects by fulfilling these needs: 

- irreconcilable and conflicting market thesis and management styles. 
- Apart from alleviating conflicts, it serves the purposes of reducing churn amongst actively contributing volunteers in our DAO community
- Forking ensures all prior contributors' efforts are ackowledged and equitably accounted in such situations
- creates more surface area for more volunteers to support DAO mission and purpose to fight "Fake News"
- reduce communication overhead and excessive efforts in aligning ever growing number of contributions in a project
- spreads DAO risk over multiple projects as opposed to consolidating all eggs in one basket (project)
- allow DAO to remain decentralized while still enjoying the benefit of a strong core leadership for each project

Soft forked project 
- Allows a parent project to "theorectically" sponsor a child project. 
- Contributions to a child project is still recorded on the parent project's ledger but labelled differently
- Contributions to the child project are still awarded governance tokens of the parent project
- Revenue generated by child project are held in the parent project vault

Hard forked project 
- Child project has claim independence of parent project
- Contributions to a child project is recorded on its own branced off version of the paren project's ledger
- Contributions to the child project are awarded governacen tokens in the child project.
- Revenue generated by child project are held in its own project vault

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
The value of Beer Hall

- a place to surface unknown unknowns via discussion. A lot of the topics surfaced here ends up becoming trends that inform what potential projects to pursue next

- a place where members of the DAO can come together to get to interact with each other in a generally informal setting

-  a place where useful information about DAO operations can be surfaced, discussed upon and eventually voted upon

- a place where members can have visibility into the kind of value that is exchange hands between various DAO members. In other spaces, a lot of these kind of exchanges are done in privacy so other members who might be able to jump in to participate ends up missing out because they don't know the deal flow is happening. In fact most of the introductions I made, they are done here in this channel except those that have some NDA concerns in place.

*Proposed governance token management protocol*

The purpose of this protocol is to discourage excessive speculation on our governance tokens in the open market once it gets listed on Centralized exchanges while at the same time capitalize on market fluctuations to increased our fiat netbook value per issued governance token ratio



*_Rules_*
    - _*Rule 1*_: every quarter DAO will make provisions to increase governance tokens in circulation by 25% of what is already in circulation last day of the previous quarter. 

    - _*Rule 2*_: Full amount might not end up being circulated in the market if no exceptional price ranges present themselves 

    - _*Rule 3*_: DAO will make open market purchase as and when market value at which governance token is traded at falls below USDT net book value. 

    - _*Rule 4*_: DAO will make open market sales of governance tokens up to the total provision specified for market circulation as and when market value per token exceeds the minimal of either USDT1 or USDT net book value per token



*_Conclusion_* 
This protocol for governance token management when strictly adhered to in the long haul is anti-dilutive on nature. 

It has the effect of discouraging excessive speculation activities beyond desirable price range both on the upside and the downside 

The muting of speculative components in open market pricing of DAO governance token help curtail distractions DAO governance token holders might otherwise experience away from daily practice of Satseva

My thoughts regarding all these recent discussions about commission from sales of cacao nibs…

Here is a good analogy… 

All these chefs in the kitchen are spending alot of cycles debating on the size of the shovel the gardeners working on the farm in the backyard should be using 

Meanwhile none of the chefs in the kitchen have  ever the intent of actually rolling up their sleeves to dig a hole in the farm using the shovel or have ever done so.

After observing the above described episode and then observing how things were done in the Zen monastery as well as recalling how logistics in the Singapore military was ran during my 2.5 years there see below. 

*Key takeaways*
- saying don’t do this or that, but not stating clearly what exactly needs to be done is not helpful. Except for the purpose of entertainment during free time, it almost definitely a waste of time reading the text

- ⁠surface rules that are objective, measurable and positive 

- ⁠surface actual rules that could be compiled together to define a recipe/protocol/policy that could be executed step by step, tested and then fine tuned

- ⁠person surfacing rules for compilation into recipe/protocol/policy should be one who have actually rolled up sleeves and dug a hole or is about to start digging a hole with a shovel. definitely not by folks who are solely intent on just hanging around in the kitchen speculating what size of hole that is to be dug on the farm and what size shovel 

- ⁠for everyone to feel included, once the gardeners have surfaced the recipe/protocol/policy for voting, everyone feel free to cast your vote 

- ⁠when someone surfaces a rule, critically access the signal from the noise. 

- ⁠signal: from person who is truly intent on digging the hole or has already dug one. 

- ⁠noise: from person who is just speculating and has no intention of doing so

*Examples of what are rules and what are not*

_Valid proposed rule_
- for each additional 1 centimeters of width in a hole, the depth needs to be increased by 2 centimeters. 
- ⁠For holes deeper than 10 centimeters, please use large shovel. 
- ⁠For holes lesser than 10 centimeters, please use small shovel. 


_Invalid proposed rules_
- the hole needs to be big. (_what do you mean by big_)

@16468233438 I relooked into our costing of our most recent shipment from Brazil into USA

*Cost of the goods itself*
- 100KG cacao nibs: $R6500 = USD1,310.3846

*Cost of the transportation and customs* 
- _Leitl Express_ - Trucking from Ilheus to Salvador: $R1066.85 = USD215.11019
- _Omega Services_ - Air Freight from Salvador to SF Airport: $R4000 = USD806.53795
- _SeaCoast Logistics_ - Custom Clearance at SF Airport: USD561.03

If our goal is to bring cost per KG down to USD20 and still pay the farmers the fair price they are asking for than shipping and freighting cost needs to go down. 

Four options to optimize our supply chain bound for USA
- ⁠Find cheaper freight forwarding company
- ⁠Do sea freight instead of air freight
- Increase shipping volume to acquire economies of scale. _but first we need to decipher which cost is fixed and which cost is variable_
- ⁠Figure out how to do customs clearance ourselves to save on the USD561.03 by removing SeaCoast Logistics from the equation. _Doesn’t feel like Grazie is actually doing much for us but still charging us stuff_.

*Proposal to SF LUV from Agroverse*

*Date:* March 5, 2025  

Dear SF LUV Team,  

We are excited to introduce Agroverse, a project operated by TrueSight DAO, dedicated to regenerating 10,000 hectares of Amazon rainforest. Our mission is to support cacao farmers who practice agroforestry, helping them regrow the rainforest on formerly deforested land in the Amazonian region. By purchasing premium regenerative cacao directly from these farmers, we distribute it to conscious consumers in the USA and Europe, fostering sustainable agriculture, environmental restoration, and economic empowerment for local communities.  

We are reaching out to explore a potential collaboration with SF LUV as a merchant partner. Given our shared commitment to positive impact, we believe Agroverse’s regenerative cacao aligns well with your values. We are currently distributing in San Francisco and would love to offer your community the opportunity to purchase our cacao using the SF LUV token.  

To make this partnership seamless, we’d like to understand how we can redeem SF LUV tokens for cash after accepting them as payment for our cacao. Could you please provide details on the redemption process, including any requirements or steps involved? We’re eager to integrate this innovative payment option and deepen our impact in the San Francisco market.  

We look forward to hearing from you and exploring how we can work together to create a meaningful partnership. Please feel free to contact us at [insert contact info] for further discussion.  

Warm regards,  
Gary  
A Contributor

The first thing that came to mind this morning when I woke up and thought through all the signals gathered from the ecosystem and beyond so far is that we might have already achieved *_product market fit*_

Me and @⁨Kirsten Ritschel⁩ spent 30 minutes two evenings ago discussing about holding cacao circles here in the Bay Area while I am away. She commenting that the product is pretty much selling itself at this point 

Jerry mentioned three months ago when we were discussing the qualitative data gathered from our growth hack into local stores that it is a very very healthy sign that the sales cycle is extremely short (_in a matter of few minutes_) after presenting the call to action to venue operators who are value aligned versus infinitely long (_zero conversion_) when speaking to venue operators who are not-values aligned 

The cacao was invited into the two exclusive climate week gatherings where values aligned individuals were gathered 

From my perspective, product market fit is like deciphering if the economy is now in recession, it only becomes apparent in hindsight once you have crossed the threshold 

From a high level perspective the following is clear

- *WHY*: Regenerate our Amazon rainforest because it is important for the continued survival of our species on earth 

- ⁠*WHAT*: Bags of cacao sourced from farmers actively restoring it 

- ⁠*HOW*: still in the crowd sourced experimentation phase. And this is the current phase of where our meta-game


https://mailchimp.com/resources/product-market-fit/#:~:text=%22Product%2Dmarket%20fit%2C%22,%2C%20that's%20product%2Dmarket%20fit.

Me and @kikiscocoa spent an hour in a facetime session. Items and schedules for this year discussed 

- Summer time is a challenging time to ship chocolate as it melts.

- ⁠The state the packages arrives in San Francisco is not acceptable if we are going to ship direct to our consignees, USPS doesn't treat the cacao with the reverence that it should have. We need to improve the way we pack the cacao before it ships out of @⁨Matheus Reis - Bahia Coop⁩ warehouse in Ilheus to safeguard against that

- ⁠Exclusive cacao circles in San Francisco targeted specifically at chocolatiers in Bay Area to showcase what we have available in our warehouse. Each of this exclusive cacao circle will be restricted to just 6 participants for a cosy intimate setting much like the cacao circle we had at the Festivals up here where we got to connect with other vendors present

- ⁠The *Radical Transparency* we introduced into our supply chain is something that resonates with chocolatiers

- Chocolatiers ⁠always face the constant challenge where suppliers abandon their cacao because something else more lucrative come about

- The sales lead list gathered from San Francisco Chocolatier festival will be a great way to feed participants into our summer time exclusive cacao circles. 

- ⁠Summer time in the North is also the time to be in the Southern hemisphere as it is cacao harvesting season.

I spent 1.5 hour brewing the ice cold cacao and walking the faire grounds to offer it to vendors 

I think this approach of directly serving samples of cacao to every single vendor at their booth suggested by Atelier is more well suited for such kinds of gatherings if the intention is to acquire vendors 

Might end up being more scalable than holding cacao circles directly targeting consumers since most consumers as observed is usually a one off hence the CAC (_customer acquisition cost_) versus the LTV (_customer life time value_) is not as positive on the _Return on Capital_ deployed 

To optimize the model, you want to drive down *_CAC*_ as much as possible and target demographics with the highest possible *_LTV X Conversion rates*_ multiple 

ideally if possible drive CAC down to Zero, hence why I have been spending time doing all the trash run to get pass the gates free of charge and systematically utilizing food banks to cut down food related operating expenses

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 240
- Description: Agroverse Shop Updates
  
  Updates to the Agroverse shop:
  
  NEW EXPERIENCES ADDED
  Added two seasonal experiences to the Pacific West Coast journey where cacao is offered:
  
  • Slab City & Salvation Mountain - The Last Free Place in America
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/slab-city-salvation-mountain/index.html
  
  • Winter Desert Gatherings - Quartzite, Salton Sea & Joshua Tree
    https://agroverse.shop/cacao-journeys/pacific-west-coast-path/experiences/winter-desert-gatherings/index.html
  
  These gatherings (Tribe Boheme, Van Aid, SchooliePalooza, Bombay Beach Binnelie, Boondockers bash, Quartzite gem show, Rubber Tramp Rendezvous) occur during winter season (Thanksgiving through end of winter) and are now part of the journey map.
  
  TASTE PROFILE VISUALIZATIONS
  Added interactive taste profile charts to shipment pages. The inclusion of these taste graphs was inspired by noticing them on one of the cacao brands that Kirsten shared. Process:
  
  1. Took photos of taste profile sheets from CIC (Cacao Innovation Center)
  2. Used Grok to generate a detailed prompt
  3. Used that prompt with Cursor AI to generate the code
  4. Embedded interactive D3.js charts on each shipment page
  
  Taste profiles available on:
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl4/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl6/index.html
  https://agroverse.shop/shipments/agl8/index.html
  
  COMMUNITY COLLABORATION
  Discussed taste profiling with Matheus. Since taste is subjective, we don't need to pay CIC for this. We have a community of chocolate makers and chocolatiers in San Francisco who can be involved in the process, making it more authentic and community-driven.
  
  THOUGHTS ON AI & WEB EVOLUTION
  Observations on web evolution:
  
  • Web 1.0 (Geocities era) - Rich, handcrafted pages, complex ecosystem
  • Web 1.5 (MySpace) - Mix of handcrafted and templated
  • Web 2.0 (Facebook) - Everything templatized for scale
  • Web 3.0 (AI era) - AI could handcraft pages, bringing back Web 1.0 richness without the heavy human lifting... the only question is a site fully ran based on this paradigm can it be scalable
  
  Experimenting with AI as a creative partner to build unique, handcrafted experiences at scale. The taste profile charts are an example - each tailored to the specific shipment without manually coding every one.

raw_contributions.Contribution Made:
[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 120
- Description: Got this repository up and running so that future LLMs on other machines can easily come up to speed on context to handle various tasks within our DAO ecoystem
  
  https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/agentic_ai_context
  
  Basically human getting AIs to teach AIs so that humans dont need to teach again
  
  Started experimenting with the following come online based LLMs as opposed to cursor AI for eventual deployment to the cloud
  
  - Gemini CLI
  - ⁠Grok CLI
  - ⁠Claude CLI
  - ⁠Codex CLI
  
  Spent some time thinking through the architecture of how other RAG (_Retreival Augmentation Generation_) infrastructure have been set up 
  
  My sense is instead of incurring a bunch of server cost setting up a vector space database which we don’t really need at our scale as well as the simplicity of what we are doing 
  
  Pre-compile all our DAO’s knowledge based data as vectors and index them as flat files. 
  
  When we need the LLM to make specialized decisions within our context, just have one of the servers convert a query that is being passed in by the user into a vector and do a Euclidean comparison of the query versus all the other factors in the index files to retrieve the right contacts and then pass them to LLM we are utilizing to get the final result to return to the user.
  
  And if the data size becomes a little larger, we just shove the pre-compound vectors into an SQL light database, which is due a flat file that can be easily ported from one server to another. 
  
  Recurring modes of usage that I can think of 
  
  - on boarding of new prospective members
  - ⁠ existing members who wants to get caught up on what has happened in the DAO recently
  - ⁠ freight and shipping configurations
  - ⁠ production cost optimization configurations
  - ⁠ go to market and store outreach strategy
  - ⁠ stores re-stocking strategy
  - ⁠ social media content, marketing ongoing efforts and strategy
  
  My sense is once the stack is implemented. I got to spend less time on all this stuff that requires a lot of logic and just kinda mechanical and perhaps repetitive. 
  
  Instead spend more time on face-to-face interactions for business development and trust building purposes.

Caught + fixed an aws_query response-envelope bug via a live probe.

- Description: truesight_autopilot — sophia HSTS + self-deploy hardening (PRs #75 + #76 + #77)
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/75
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/76

  Details:
  Two questions from Gary, both shipped:
  
  1. 'How do we ensure the deploy script ran is always the latest?' → Self-deploy hit an in-memory caching bug when fixes to the deploy flow itself didn't take effect until the NEXT invocation (because Python imports deploy.py once at module load).
  
     PR #76 fixes this with a two-phase re-exec pattern: phase-one (parent) does git pull then spawns a fresh Python subprocess with env-var sentinel AUTOPILOT_DEPLOY_PHASE=phase_two_post_pull. Child re-imports deploy.py from disk (now containing whatever the pull brought in), runs pip install + restart + nginx, returns JSON to parent stdout. Parent stays alive so /chat callers get the response cleanly.
  
     Subsequent self-deploy then surfaced PR #77 — certbot --nginx edits /etc/nginx/sites-available/sophia which is symlinked into the repo, so the next git pull refuses to merge the dirty state. Fix: replace git pull with git fetch + reset --hard origin/main + clean -fd (matching scripts/deploy.sh).
  
  2. 'How do we get sophia behind https without the Not secure error?' → TLS itself was correct (valid Let's Encrypt cert, working 80→443 redirect), but HSTS header was missing so browsers tried http:// first on every visit, briefly showing 'Not secure'.
  
     PR #75 adds Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload to sophia.conf. After first HTTPS visit, browsers cache the HSTS rule for 2 years and skip the http:// hop entirely.
  
  Validated end-to-end:
  - Self-deploy returned status=success, 4 steps OK, in 15.0s on a dirty repo state

  - Both systemd units active, /health=ok

  Details:
  Shipped V1 of the credential vault Gary asked for: 'if I fuck up my MacBook I can restore the entire context/everything easily.' Scope = ~46 credential files across ~/Applications/*/{.env,config/,credentials/}, ~/.clasprc-*.json, ~/.config/gh/, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/ — everything not in any git repo.
  
  Architecture:
  - Explicit allowlist manifest (CREDENTIAL_MANIFEST.txt) — no globs, auditable.
  - backup_credentials.sh tars manifest paths and pipes through openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -iter 600000 with a 0600 passphrase file (LastPass-managed).
  - Output lands in ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/credential_vault/ with 30-snapshot retention + credentials-latest.age symlink.

  Details:
  Gary couldn't sign in to https://edgar.truesight.me/users/sign_in via Google. Google was returning 'Access blocked: Authorization Error / Error 400: invalid_request / doesn't comply with Google's OAuth 2.0 policy for keeping apps secure' — the generic policy banner that masks the actual reason.
  
  Diagnosis path:
  1. First read of the symptom suggested the OAuth consent screen's homepage / privacy URLs were dead (https://getdata.io returned HTTP 000 — connection refused). Steered Gary to console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials/consent for project 667737028020 (the legacy GetData.IO GCP project that owns the OAuth client krake_ror_prod, which Edgar reuses).
  2. Gary checked the OAuth Client page first (where redirect URIs and JS origins live) — those were correctly configured: https://edgar.truesight.me + https://edgar.truesight.me/users/auth/google_oauth2/callback both present. 'Last used date: May 6, 2026' confirmed the client was working as recently as 5 days ago — so the client config wasn't the problem.
  3. Asked Gary to click 'see error details' link on the Google error page. The actual error was: 'redirect_uri=/users/auth/google_oauth2/callback flowName=GeneralOAuthFlow'. Critical insight — the redirect_uri being SENT to Google was a RELATIVE PATH with no host. A relative path can never match the absolute https://edgar.truesight.me/... URLs registered on the OAuth client, so Google rejects with the policy banner.
  4. Verified the infrastructure side was clean:
     - DNS edgar.truesight.me -> 3.90.179.151 (autopilot seni_ror_new) ✓
     - Authoritative Route53 record matches ✓
     - nginx config on seni_ror_new sets proxy_set_header Host  + X-Forwarded-Proto https ✓
     - config/environments/production.rb has google_client_id + google_client_secret correctly set
     - Edgar service active, port 3002 listening ✓
     So nginx wasn't dropping headers — the issue had to be on the Rails side.
  5. Found the gap: OmniAuth was relying on Rack request inspection to construct the full URL, and that fell through to a path-only result behind the new nginx setup. Devise/omniauth-google-oauth2 doesn't auto-set OmniAuth.config.full_host; you must do it explicitly OR set config.action_controller.default_url_options. Edgar had only config.action_mailer.default_url_options set (for email URL helpers), which doesn't help OmniAuth.
  
  Sentiment_importer PR #1054 (merged + deployed):
  - New config/initializers/omniauth.rb sets OmniAuth.config.full_host = ENV['EDGAR_FULL_HOST'].presence || 'https://edgar.truesight.me' in production. Override-able via env var for a future staging environment.
  - Ran ./deploy.sh --skip-migrate against seni_ror_new + seni_sk_new; both came up cleanly (port 3002 healthy, Sidekiq active).
  - Bypasses Rack header inspection entirely so the OAuth flow no longer depends on subtle nginx forwarding behavior — robust against future infra changes.
  
  Separate concerns surfaced during diagnosis (not addressed in this PR — flagged for follow-up):
  1. Edgar runs as 'rails s -e production' (single-threaded WEBrick). nginx error log on seni_ror_new shows clusters of 'upstream prematurely closed connection' 502s — bot scan traffic on /companies/STWD and other heavy routes is choking the single-process server. Worth migrating to Puma + workers (the Gemfile.lock shows puma is already a dependency).
  2. config/environments/production.rb has the OAuth client_id AND client_secret hardcoded in git history. Lower priority than getting auth working but worth rotating the secret and moving to ENV / systemd-drop-in (same pattern used for CURRENCY_CONVERSION_WEBHOOK_URL in the recent migration).
  3. The OAuth client lives in a dead Krake/GetData.IO GCP project. Cleaner long-term: create a new OAuth 2.0 Client ID under a TrueSight-DAO-owned GCP project, retire the krake_ror_prod client.

[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 90
- Description: Edgar OAuth post-mortem: nginx $host heredoc trap fixed + documented
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/agentic_ai_context/pull/120
  
  Details:
  Diagnosed and resolved the 4-hour Edgar OAuth outage on edgar.truesight.me.
  
  ## Symptom
  After PR #1054 (OmniAuth.config.full_host) shipped, Google's OAuth consent screen
  worked, but every Devise redirect endpoint (/users/sign_in, /users/sign_out,
  post-OAuth callback, /companies/:slug) returned 502 Bad Gateway. Static landing
  page kept working.
  
  ## Root cause (compound bug)
  1. Yesterday's migration to TRUESIGHT_DAO_AUTOPILOT created the new nginx
     config via a single-quoted bash heredoc that contained backslash-escaped
     variables — \$host, \$request_uri, etc. Single-quoted heredocs do NOT
     expand variables, so the backslashes were preserved verbatim in the file.
     nginx then parsed \$host as literal '\' + variable $host, and forwarded
     'Host: \edgar.truesight.me' upstream. Rails read that as the host, every
     redirect_to became 'https://\edgar.truesight.me/...', webrick raised
     URI::InvalidURIError, nginx returned 502.
  2. Compounding bug: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/edgar.conf was a regular file
     (not a symlink to sites-available/), so the first scp+install fix to
     sites-available/ did not propagate. Re-symlinked sites-enabled, reloaded
     nginx, verified clean Host header via tcpdump, confirmed all redirect
     endpoints return clean 302s.
  
  ## Fix shipped
  - TrueSightDAO/agentic_ai_context PR #120: Documents both the heredoc trap
    and the sites-enabled symlink check in NOTES_sentiment_importer.md, plus
    updates the topology table to reflect the post-migration TRUESIGHT_DAO_AUTOPILOT
    hosts (seni_ror_new 3.90.179.151 / seni_sk_new 54.163.216.235).
  - Live nginx config on seni_ror_new restored to the clean version
    (proxy_set_header Host $host; with no backslash) and sites-enabled
    re-linked to sites-available.
  
  ## Verification
  curl -sI https://edgar.truesight.me/companies/KWR
    -> HTTP/2 302
    -> Location: https://edgar.truesight.me/users/sign_in   (no backslash)
  
  journalctl -u seni_ror: no more URI::InvalidURIError after the fix.

  Details:
  Closed the manual gap between 'draft sent in Gmail' and 'Partner Check-ins tab updated.' Without this v0.1, LLM advisors and the bell would keep recommending pokes for partners Gary had just emailed because the operator hadn't yet manually filed the check-in.
  
  ## What shipped
  - PartnerPokeDrafts.gs now has runProcessSentPartnerPokes() — new public function clasp-pushed to the live Apps Script project (14gKJ0VW49RsSn4S03pgxKXy0sp4Z7Z3Wm1Wj8jQiWW5dj1sFuPnp95sh).
  - Menu item 'Process sent pokes (auto-checkin)' added to the spreadsheet menu.
  - agentic_ai_context PR #130 (merged) — full v0.1 architecture, design choices, idempotency convention, status enum, and operator setup instructions captured in PARTNER_POKE_SCHEDULER_v0.md.
  
  ## Architecture
  Scans Partner Poke Drafts audit log for rows with status='draft_created':
  - Draft still exists in Gmail → skip (try again next run).
  - Draft gone + matching Sent message (in:sent label:AI/Partner Poke to:<email> newer_than:14d, exact subject match):
    - If is_self_poke=true → mark log row 'sent_self_poke' (no check-in filed; actual partner contact hasn't happened).
    - Else → append Partner Check-in row (Method=Email, Stock Status=Unknown, Next Check-in Date BLANK, Update ID=poke-auto-<draft_id>, Submitted By='Partner Poke Scheduler v0.1'); mark log 'sent_and_filed'.
  - Draft gone + no matching Sent message → mark log 'discarded' with note.
  
  ## Key design choices
  - Idempotency via Update ID = poke-auto-<draft_id> on Partner Check-ins col K (same dedup convention as the human-driven scanner). Re-running the scanner over the same audit row is a no-op once the check-in is filed.
  - Next Check-in Date stays BLANK by design — operator-driven cadence stays in operator's hands; auto-row records what happened, not what the operator intends. Operator files a follow-up entry manually when there's a reply or a chosen next-check-in date.
  - Self-poke drafts get a different status ('sent_self_poke') without a check-in entry — because sending the reminder to yourself doesn't constitute partner contact. The check-in is filed when Gary later acts on the offline channel.

       '[ \\t]*([^\\n]*)' — match spaces/tabs only, allow empty capture.

       transactions. Now captures beforeAppendLastRow, SpreadsheetApp.flush() after each

  ## What changed

  - **list_directory tool** (#15) — new filesystem tool to discover files in local directories
  - **Grok vision fallback** (#16) — when pyzbar/zbarimg find no codes, Grok vision model attempts to read QR codes from images

  - **BigModel (ZhipuAI/GLM-4.5) LLM provider** — new provider with automatic DeepSeek fallback; ~20x cheaper than DeepSeek
  - **Deploy script key parity check** — aborts deployment if production-only `.env` keys would be lost

[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 10
- Description: Noticed this pattern of circles and how it correlates strongly with successful partnership. Claude suggest to visit Queen Hippie Gypsy for some field work to understand what circle actually means.
  
  The pattern is: field exposure → noticed
      anomaly → hypothesis → tooling that can scale-test it. The crawl is the last step, not the first.
                  
      A few things worth flagging:
  
      1. The 14% positive rate is meaningful. Not every retailer hosts circles, but a meaningful minority do, and the early crawl
      confirms they cluster in the segment we already partner with well (Queen Hippie Gypsy, Way Home Shop, Esalen, Twisted
      Thistle). That's a real filter, not just a vanity tag.
      2. Summer's interrupted explanation is unfinished business. She was about to tell you why circles matter to her shop and got
      pulled away. That's the highest-leverage 10-minute conversation to revisit on your next visit — what role does the circle play
       in her economics? Community building? A way to get people in the door? A revenue stream? The answer probably tells you
      whether circle-hosting causes cacao velocity or just correlates with shops that are good at this category in general.
      3. The methodological pattern generalizes. Worth keeping a running list of "shops that surprised me on a visit" — Queen Hippie
       Gypsy onboarding in 5 minutes is itself a signal that's worth examining. What about her was different from the slow ones?
      That's another fieldwork-derived hypothesis to test once you have a few more data points.
      4. Don't over-rotate yet. One observation that pattern-matches a prior intuition feels great but is exactly when confirmation
      bias is strongest. The OPEN_FOLLOWUPS gate — wait for 4 partners-velocity refreshes before acting — is the right discipline.
      Resist the urge to rebuild outreach strategy around circles before the data confirms the hypothesis at scale.
  
      The teacher analogy is apt: the lesson-plan insight wasn't actionable until you understood why it worked
      (curriculum-from-scratch is the dominant pain). Same here — the next step isn't "target circle-hosting shops harder," it's
      "find out why circles matter to them economically." That's a Summer conversation, not a script.

  Details:
  ## Governor Chatbot Service — Phase 1 Deployment
  
  Built and deployed a conversational AI interface for TrueSight DAO governors. The chatbot runs on EC2 (via seni_ror), proxies to Grok (xAI) for inference, and is accessible at `chatbot.truesight.me`.
  
  ### What was built
  
  **Backend (`governor_chatbot_service`)**
  - FastAPI scaffold with health, auth, chat, and admin endpoints
  - RSA signature verification using existing DApp keypairs (WebCrypto SPKI)
  - JWT session tokens (30-min expiry, HTTP-only cookies)
  - Governor registry reads live from `treasury-cache/dao_members.json` (auto-updated on every email verification + daily cron)
  - Restricted to architect-only (Gary Teh, 30 active public keys); deny-all fallback for unauthorized keys
  - Full workspace context ingestion: 11 canonical markdown files loaded into Grok system prompt
  - Grok integration via xAI API (`grok-3-latest`)
  - DAO submission tool scaffold (Phase 2)
  - systemd service + nginx reverse proxy config + one-command install script
  
  **Frontend (`dapp/chat.html`)**
  - WebCrypto RSA signing with existing DApp keypair
  - JWT session handling with automatic refresh
  - Full Markdown rendering via marked.js CDN
  - Access-denied UI for non-governors with clear messaging
  - Container layout fixes to prevent overflow
  - Production API endpoint pointing to `https://chatbot.truesight.me`
  
  **Deployment**
  - Service running on `seni_ror` (54.211.179.126:8000)
  - nginx on `krake_ng` proxies `chatbot.truesight.me` → backend
  - SSL via existing `STAR_truesight_me.crt` wildcard
  
  ### Commits (direct-pushed to `main`)
  
  **`TrueSightDAO/governor_chatbot_service`**
  - `5bc1404` — Initial scaffold (Phase 1 + Phase 2)
  - `94dca97` — Governor registry via GitHub raw URL + caching
  - `4e7e540` — Use treasury-cache `dao_members.json` as live registry
  - `eebb5c7` — Deploy scripts (systemd, nginx, install)
  
  **`TrueSightDAO/dapp`**
  - `dcae305` — Governor Chat page + nav link
  - `4dc0155` — Container overflow fix
  - `d5c91d7` — Nav/badge inside container
  - `b4449e4` — Full Markdown rendering
  - `b2a577b` — Production API endpoint
  
  ### Architecture
  ```
  Browser (DApp chat.html)
      ↓ HTTPS + RSA-signed messages
  krake_ng (nginx reverse proxy, SSL termination)
      ↓ proxy_pass
  seni_ror:8000 (FastAPI + Grok)
      ↓
  treasury-cache/dao_members.json (live governor registry)
  ```

  - EC2 never stores private keys; only verifies signatures

I am still thinking we should challenge this technical assumption of needing to print a minimal of 500 units for each batch

When I was in Ilheus Brazil doing inspection last year I noticed one of the facilities have their own rolls of labels for printing which means they have label printing machines available locally 

If we can figure out that part of the logistics then we can get even more creative with our supply chain

_Ideal configuration for our supply chain_

- DAO pre-finances 25 bags of cacao with custom artwork on the front of the Kraft pouch bag provided by the local community it’s being distributed in

- ⁠each comes with its own QR code

_How the $25 revenue gets distributed_

- $8 goes to local community distributor which can help finance the local community project, for example school meals in Corvallis Oregon, Mural artwork to revitalize Chinatown area in Portland Oregon

- ⁠$5 goes for tree planting 

- ⁠$10 goes to the farmers and the manufacturers for their cacao

- ⁠$2 goes back to DAO to finance the exchange of voting rights to USD if there is interest

This is as micro and as localized as possible for the various communities

entries.contribution:
Synchronicity. 

Rather than utilizing a wallet service provided by a third party, brands are opting to launch their own digital wallet solution that brand supporters can use. 

Based on my understanding of their technology, they are also managing the underlying layer where user data is stored 

https://cdcgaming.com/brief/caesars-entertainment-launches-universal-digital-wallet-in-nevada/

Rather than utilizing the phantom wallet and the underlying solana chain which we have no effective way manage if things goes wrong which I have observed on quite a few occasions, not just this recent hack, it makes better sense for our community to build and manage our own stack 

After closely monitoring the MetaMask Wallet which I also had installed on my browser, it seems the hacker was not able to access it even though the browser information associated with it was taken. This just means that phantom wallet security was not properly implemented

I think the current 
https://dapp.truesight.me 

And the underlying chat logs and Google sheets is a good way to move forward for now 

https://truesight.me/ledger

We don’t get charged for every single transaction we make in our community 

If anything goes wrong we could always just do the necessary adjustments on the google sheet and since it’s public everyone could review it

entries.contribution:
This is a framework that I forgot to mention that just came to mind that I used as a lens through which to think about DAO models during the early days 

the concept is described  in the book *_finite and infinite games*_ which I found sitting on a table one day 

The equivalent of finite games in our ecosystem from my perspective are the various initiatives like @⁨<guild>[initiative] Agroverse⁩ @⁨<guild>[initiative] SunMint Guild⁩ and @⁨Edgar  ⁩ 

From my perspective these are transient, their continued existence without our ecosystem is highly dependent on participants continued willingness to play them.  

The infinite game within the context of our DAO are the current rules we have in place for the tokenization of DAO member contributions. 

The rules as they are now are simple and generic enough for people to understand but at the same time flexible enough to allow participants the space to discover the finite games they want to play amongst themselves within the scope of this infinite game (_or what we refer to as the *Meta Game* in our White Paper_)

When me and @⁨Tomas - Offchain⁩ first sat down together three years ago in Buenos Aires to further explore game dynamics, the ecosystem was not yet matured enough to such an extend the finite games are aggregating real world assets to such an extend the in-game tokens of our infinite games had any material value. Back then no one really cared about the infinite game that some active participants were playing in their own heads. 

Fast forward to the present day, our in-game tokens now have actual monetary value associated with it. 

And it seems more and more external observers are awakening to the value of such infinite games and are seeking to replicate these into their own industrial verticals

An interesting idea surface within this book is how *_Evil is defined*_ 

Evil within the context of this book is defined as deliberately restricting another player’s ability to engage in the infinite game. 

From my perspective, this is where our DAO’s model start drastically differing from other DAO models out there 

bulk of existing DAO models out there are primarily centered around requiring proposals to pass via voting before associated actions are allowed, which is by design very constraining

There is very little voting events within our DAO’s model, the generic and flexible rules of our infinite game are generally permissible of any action DAO members can possibly conceive of when attempting to contribute.  

Structurally our model is more like a fly wheel which will keep just rotating so long as even a single member makes a contribution of any form. 

So the *_concept of Evil*_ as defined in the book is by design constrained from taking roots within the DAO ecosystem. And any attempt to introduce this conception of *Evil* into the ecosystem will just be met with frustration. 🤔🤣

I was thinking through the experience i had last week at the natural products expo in LA and the follow up experience I had with the nomads in the desert 

It is quite hard to envision members taking time away from their full-time jobs supporting the cacao project by standing behind the booths at expos like these for multiple days enthusiastically attempting to attract distributors to want to carry our Cacao

The vibration just did not feel right

Sharing of the Cacao in community settings and gatherings just felt more organic and natural to how members of our community would act

That’s when it occurred to me Michael Porter theory on strategy and differentiation

We are at heart a community largely motivated by our commonly shared values, and not a company with purely a profit-driven motive

As such, we should differentiate our community distribution network by focusing on what is only possible via community centric approaches, and as much as possible stay away from conventional profit centric corporate approaches to sharing with the wider community

entries.contribution:
*Problem statement 1*

Some random thoughts after attending the Natural Produce Expo to finally study end to end how conventional food distribution system works 

- large scale mono culture Farming
- ⁠aggregator 
- ⁠exporter
- ⁠freighter 
- ⁠importer 
- ⁠distributor 
- ⁠retailer 
- ⁠customers 

Right now everything from farming all the way to retailing end points seems geared for large scale operations. 

Because of this gearing, at all stages of the food distribution network as well as for the new food products productions themselves, we are forced by design to geared to require initial deployment of large volumes of capital to achieve economies of scale at some point 

- the world produces enough food to feed everybody 

- ⁠distribution is the problem 

- ⁠to achieve economies of scale trade offs are forced into the system

- current distribution system is geared for large volume of generic food products 

- ⁠ large scale single genotype monoculture is a by product of this economies of scale 

- ⁠monoculture production results in single genotype and makes supply chain vulnerable to diseases out break 

- ⁠large scale and centralized food distribution results in need for large volume of capital to be able to manufacture large quantities to push any new product through the traditional highly centralized distribution network where there are only a few gate keepers

- ⁠requirements for large capital results in need for external funding sources like those from Wall Street
 
- ⁠because distribution is large volume across large distance a lot of none-biodegradable materials are used in the package process 

- ⁠Wall Street funding forces companies to focus of share holder returns and ever increasing profit margins which means substituting Whole Foods for cheaper and less nutrient rich food ingredients 

- ⁠large scale production of volume means need to rent large commercial warehousing and storage spaces 

The really interesting question to ask is would it be possible to figure out an alternate model for food production and distribution that turns all these assumptions on its head, thereby negating the need for economies of scale, huge volumes of capital, centralized control, large scale mono-culture, utilization of large volumes of non-biodegradable packaging materials while at the same time still fulfilling the caloric and nutrient requirements of the entire human race??

- small volume
- ⁠decentralized 
- ⁠minimal packaging 
- ⁠huge diversity in food genotype within the agriculture

_Insight 1: Method of Truth Seeking_

The hippie route tends to be very unstructured, haphazard and disorganized. Things tend to fall apart

If presented with an opportunity to experience something novel and potentially pleasurable, the same behavioral change might  be more likely to occur. The best is if the cost of the behavioral change is negligible compared to the received benefit 

It is costly to be a confrontational environmental activist flying down to the Amazon rainforest and staging a demonstration by tying yourself to a tree to prevent it from being cut down

New Onchain Proposal voting event
Proposed changes to the way our network’s gas fee is calculated

https://app.realms.today/dao/2yH36PrWii3RthpHtdJVYaPgBzfcSLe7oevvGRavrut7/proposal/BuPC3Ufen6PCyXvgoYuFx498ut99a7W4ZFDeHmcwtRDq

- Current Formula: Maximum of (1 - price of our $TDG token, 1 month USA Treasury Yield )
- New Formula: Minimum of (price of our $TDG token, 1)

Reasons:

1. Bulk of DAO members are token holders and don’t really trade on the tokens. People actively selling their tokens are residents of developing countries seeking to make a livelihood through the active contributions instead of holding it for speculation purposes. 

2. When they sell the tokens, the price will fall and gas fee should fall to reflect the change in stake, this encourages more people to utilize the network for transacting cacao for their own needs

3. When revenue by the network increases, token prices will increase, encouraging people living in developing countries who need to cash out to cash out 

4. When price of token goes above one and none of the existing token holders are cashing, then DAO can do an open market sale of tokens to bring it back within range thereby increasing available resources in our vault to conduct on our asset transactions

5. Finally this new formula is easier to explain compared to the old one which becomes a mouthful after a while

*Statistics from today’s drum circle experiment at hippie hill* 

- total visually present at the park: 100
- ⁠total active participants in the drum circle: 50
- ⁠total participants that came up for a conversation and grabbed a drink: 10
- ⁠total donors: 2
- ⁠total amount raised: $13

- ⁠3 new Instagram followers to my personal account 

- ⁠1 new Instagram follower to our Agroverse account 

*Ingredients used*
- ⁠1/2 galleons of water
- ⁠1 bottle of oat milk

*Qualitative observations*

- the banner doesn’t work well outdoors 

- ⁠sales of cacao nibs bags might not work

- ⁠ people mistook the bags as complementary
 
- ⁠one attempted to open the bag 

- ⁠a second was trying to bargain for a free bag
 
- ⁠it was obvious the second had mental health issues 

- ⁠there is a distinct demographic difference between seekers (_utilizing discomfort as opportunity for practice_) and hippies (_just want to be free from all discomfort_) 

- ⁠doing the capoeira right in the middle of the drum circle when invited to dance was Hit, upon successful ice breaking, rate of stranger to conversation increased drastically thereafter so is total number of people attempting to visit booth
 
- ⁠we did not have enough cacao to serve them

- ⁠the banner knocked over the cacao and spilled half when the wind blew 

- ⁠people felt the recipe was too thin

- ⁠some suggested to add spice like cinnamon to fill up the gaps in the drink

- ⁠the hot Cacau was not hot enough
- despite not having the banner on display, the two laminated panels on the container held drew curiosity 

- ⁠not all people are familiar that Amazon also refers to the rainforest. Some thought I work for Amazon the company 

- ⁠some from the community are expecting me to pop by again next Sunday

I spent 6.5 hours setting up and then conducting the experiment

Finally the matter discussed with Fatima for a good one hour clicked in my head as an actionable heuristic

*_Issue identified*_
Being highly opinionated does not equate to strong follow through ability. 

We have observed a large enough sample size within our DAO to draw this conclusion. 

And here is how our core value translates into operating process 

*Old process based on outdated core value* 

- outdated core value: integrity

- ⁠process: if someone in DAo claims he can do something better, we default assume the integrity in his claim, he is allowed to freely take over an existing process that might already be working and execute the change 

- ⁠usual observation: working process after being taken over, gets mismanaged. Highly opinionated individual realizes he cannot undertake the task. Silently craps out without informing other DAO members to save face 

- ⁠second order impact: other members who might already have been contributing to priorly working process gets discouraged and drops out. Can’t even reinstate priorly working process at this point 

*New process based on updated core value*

- updated core value: Trustlessness

- process: highly opinionated individual might claim he can take over an existing process and do it better. DAO member overseeing the existing working process should bluntly state, he doesn’t trust this highly opinionated individual. The highly opinionated individual can be granted a small restricted scope to proof he can actually deliver. His scope is gradually allowed to increase as he continues to prove his competence

entries.contribution:
Thoughts on the challenge posed by Sujit on _why not just use one of those regular open sourced inventory management systems that could be had off the Internet?_ 
 
If and when industrialization of space becomes possibility, a blockchain based decentralized inventory management will become a necessity as opposed to one with a centralized database   

Imagine a space ship transporting production from a heavy industry manufacturing facility from one of the larger asteroids somewhat far way to earth. Trying to call Earth’s internet to make an update one of the databases running on one of its servers will be a total pain in the ass every time a supply run occurs 

Makes sense to have a more GitHub like protocol where every time a ship arrives back on earth, it can hook up to the earth’s network and do a sync of the ledger reflecting the inventory status on the far flung asteroid

narrative.text: Gary Teh serves as a current member of the Board of Governors for TrueSight DAO. His contributions span projects including Agroverse, Sun Mint, AID framework, Cypher Defense, Edgar, FORK, MarketMonocle, MoNYtyze L1 Protocol, MoonShot, Real Estate on Chains, Recurring Tokenizations, Rotten Radish, The ArtTalk Magazine, Trinity, TrueSight DAO, and TrueSight.Me, with primary focus on human effort hours, liquidity provision, offline commerce tasks, and build game operations such as attending FaceTime meetings and consolidating materials from discussions. Active from 20171231 to 20260430, Gary has participated in three sessions (40 minutes total) of the TrueSight Capoeira program under the Tribo Bahia Mirim lineage, rooted in Bico Duro.
